notes:
## Box fit

The player box now measures the character instead of guessing.

- The old box was a fixed 5.6-stud slab lifted off the root, so it sat inside the rig: too short over the head, too narrow around the arms.
- The box is now the character's own AABB, gathered from the body parts, re-measured four times a second so a swinging arm or a fishing cast grows it instead of clipping through it.
- Equipped gear is excluded from the measurement - a rod held out to the side no longer drags the box off the body - and the head carries a crown allowance so hooded and custom avatars are covered instead of cut.
- Eight AABB corners are projected through the view matrix and the screen rectangle is the bound of those points. A single distance plus a fixed aspect only fits when the camera looks square at the model; up close or off to one side the near corners project further out, and that is what made the box slide and shrink.
- Box scale now trims or pads the fitted rectangle.

## Camera lock

The box sat one frame behind the camera: sweep the view and it trailed to the side, then snapped back when the turn stopped.

- The view matrix is sampled as late in the frame as possible, after the per-target reads instead of before them.
- **Camera lock** advances the matrix by one frame using the measured frame-to-frame delta, scaled by the actual frame time and capped, so a long frame cannot overshoot into a bounce.
- Player markers are no longer eased: the position is read every frame, so the box is placed with this frame's value. Smoothing stays on the fish, where a scan is a 200 ms sample.

## Cards

Every card with a master switch in its head dims its settings when the switch is off - not just the extras tab and not just the fish card. The rule matches the switch itself, so a new card inherits it the moment it is added.

Version 1.1.15.
